options.explanation: That's the numbers themselves, not their counts of 1 bits.
The list covers 0..n inclusive (n + 1 entries), starting with bits[0] = 0.
4 is 100 (one set bit) and 5 is 101 (two), so the last two are 1 and 2.

workedExample:
`i >> 1` drops the last bit (already computed), and `i & 1` adds it back if it was a 1.

```
i  bin  i>>1  bits[i>>1]  i&1  bits
0  000  -     -           -    0
1  001  0     0           1    1
2  010  1     1           0    1
3  011  1     1           1    2
4  100  2     1           0    1
5  101  2     1           1    2
```

O(n) table operations in the word model (n is the largest number, here 5), versus O(n log n) operations overall for bit-at-a-time or Kernighan loops over 0..n. Hardware popcount and arbitrary-precision Python have different operation costs.
